transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. As part of our normal prepayment review for the proposed $8,000,000 voluntary loan prepayment this quarter, I need to check with each of you before I make the binding treasury decision. We have $18,000,000 in unrestricted cash, a $10,000,000 term loan at 7.2%, and a $5,000,000 interest-rate swap paired with it. I'd like to hear from lender relations, treasury forecasting, and tax accounting -- is there anything affecting this transaction that I should know about?

transcript.text: I received a lender email this morning that's critical to this transaction. The lender confirmed that the prepayment fee is waived ONLY if the company prepays exactly $6,000,000 -- not $8,000,000. The email also confirms that a $6,000,000 prepayment requires no loan-amendment filing. I have not yet uploaded this email to the transaction file, but Elena, you need this before making your decision.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Elena, I need to flag a critical cash constraint before you make your decision. I completed the rolling cash forecast this morning, and it confirms that $7,250,000 of unrestricted cash must remain as the operating reserve through quarter-end due to scheduled payroll, tax, and supplier outflows. That means only $10,750,000 of the $18,000,000 is actually available for the prepayment. An $8,000,000 prepayment would leave us at $10,000,000, which is above the reserve but leaves very thin headroom. I have not yet circulated this forecast to you, so you wouldn't have had this information until now.

transcript.text: Elena, I need to flag an important tax-accounting issue for this transaction. My tax-accounting memo, received this week, confirms that a $3,000,000 partial termination of the swap must be recorded with a $95,000 cash settlement, while the remaining $2,000,000 swap stays in place. I have not yet attached this memo to the treasury workpaper, so this wouldn't have been visible in the transaction file. This $95,000 cash settlement is an additional cash outflow that needs to be factored into the prepayment decision alongside the items Martin and Jo just raised.
